claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask you some questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I have a couple of questions about your own circumstances.

Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care (such as looking after his welfare, providing food, clothing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's a bit complicated actually. Alex has been in hospital for a while now - about 3 or 4 months. I haven't really been able to spend money on him while he's been there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's situation. I'm sorry to hear he's been in hospital.

I need to ask a few more questions about this to understand your eligibility, as there are specific rules about Child Benefit when a child is in hospital.

You mentioned Alex has been in hospital for about 3-4 months. Has this been continuous, or has he had any breaks from hospital during this time (where he came home for a period)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's been continuous - he's been in the hospital ward the whole time without coming home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Since Alex has been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks (3-4 months), there's an important follow-up question.

Have you been regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay? For example, this could include things like bringing him items, paying for activities, or other expenses related to his care or comfort.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been able to afford to spend money on him while he's been in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your situation. I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is the hospital where Alex is staying located in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it is - he's in a UK hospital.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one final question to complete the assessment.

Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, you're a UK citizen, have settled status, or have another valid immigration status that allows you to live here)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old
- He has been in a UK hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks
- You have not been regularly spending money on him during his hospital stay

Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Alex is under 16**, which would normally qualify him for Child Benefit
- However, Alex has been **in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks**
- Under the rules, after 12 weeks in hospital, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit
- There is an exception that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit if you are **regularly spending money on the child** during their hospital stay (for example, on items, activities, or comfort)
- Since you've confirmed you haven't been able to spend money on Alex during this time, this exception does not apply

**What you could do:**

If your circumstances change and you begin regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital, you may become eligible again. I would recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office to discuss your specific situation, as they can provide guidance tailored to your circumstances.

Additionally, once Alex leaves hospital and returns home to live with you, you would likely be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point.

I'm sorry this isn't better news. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
